column3: Hello, in this video I am going to explain Apache Kafka for you within 10 minutes with a simple
analogy. In my hand is an envelope and I want to ship this envelope or send this envelope
to my dear friend, Enburley and I am in UAE and I need to ship this information. How do I do that?
Well, you already know you use physical post offices to send this information to a particular
destination. How does this flow work like? Let's take a look. Let's start with the envelope itself.
So, this is a physical envelope that I had and I need to ship this information or ship this envelope
to my friend, Enburley. What is the starting point? The starting point is UAE and I am the
producer of this information and I need to send this information to my friend, Enburley, that is in
Germany. How does this whole flow look like and how is it related to Apache Kafka? Let me explain
that. This information, of course, you might ask, hey, why don't you just send a digital copy? Let's
assume that I don't and I have to send a physical copy. So, the first entry point for me is the post
office here and I give some information related to where I need to send this information.
Based on that, these people are going to route it to a right section within the post office.
For example, this section is going to Germany and this section probably is going to,
let's say, Britain or UK. And there is another section which is giving or sending all the
information or the post, so let's say Japan. So, the moment my information is collected by
the person sitting in the post office, they shall route the package itself to the right
subsection. So, my envelope lands here. So, the first step is connecting to the post office and
second step is landing it at the right queue. Of course, if you dump this data or if they put it
in a wrong place like UK, it shall never reach my friend at all. This is the segregation of the
incoming data and that is a key in Apache Kafka 2. Now, let me continue with this process itself
for now. Once you have this information, it sits there until somebody collects this or it gets shipped
in any kind or form to the final destination that would be a post office, a PO box in Germany.
Now, within Germany, again, there would be multiple places where it gets sorted and it would end up
in the Berlin section and then it would be reaching my friend in Berlin and he would be consuming
his information. This simple process, we are all aware of it. In fact, we use this day in and day
out, but you know that this itself is a backbone of Apache Kafka. Well, what do I mean by it?
This by this example, you understood four key terminologies in Apache Kafka. What are they?
Well, the person producing this envelope that is me in this case is what we call as a producer.
Then, we have the whole post office network is Apache Kafka. The backbone of our service,
it has sorting systems, it has information of every other post offices, it knows which message
came first, that is which envelope came first, who sent it, where should it go, have it kept it
properly, is there a guarantee for this or an insurance for this package, what happens if I
miss this package, everything is within the post office. Also, not just that, when you give this
envelope to the post office, they always give you an acknowledgement saying that, we have received
envelope, we are going to make sure it is going to reach the final destination. Even Apache Kafka
does that, it is called as acknowledgement services in Apache Kafka. Well, this post office itself,
whatever I explained, is a very similar way in which Apache Kafka functions. Then, we have the
end person who consume this information, which we call as consumer. So, just like how the post
office work, we have three or four important pieces, that is the producer, the Kafka as a service,
which has internal services, and then you have the consumer. Within the Kafka itself,
the segregation part that you see here is what we call as topics. Topics are basically a way in which
you segregate the incoming messages based on the application needs. And all of these topics are
present in the post box, let us say here in UAE, let us say it is in Dubai, this is a broker. A broker
is a physical server where Apache Kafka has been installed and topics can actually span
across different brokers too. Well, this is how with an analogy, you can remember how Kafka works
in a technological space too. Just like this, an event is fired by an application. So, the producer
is the application that is firing the event. It reaches a topic because all of these events
needs to be stored or segregated properly. So, they land in a topic. Where is this topic?
Is the topic having any kind of replication, guarantees, etcetera. But all of this is defined
in Apache Kafka and the Apache Kafka is installed on multiple broker set up, which are physical servers.
And then comes the consumer. In this case, the post office case, somebody went and delivered
the data to the final consumer, but in Kafka, the consumer reads this information by themselves,
and they do the processing. I hope this analogy was helpful for you to understand
how to relate Kafka to a real world example. Well, what are the four important terminologies
